messages:
alex_w: quick note — last night we paged on multiple GPU OOM alerts in eu-west-1 during an autoscale churn. severity = P2 but ~90% were transient and resolved by node restarts. thinking: switch these specific OOM alerts to ticketing unless concurrent node count drops below 10% for 5m. also add 15m regional quiet window for repeated OOMs per node-pool. any concerns?
maya_k: +1 to reducing pages for noisy OOMs. we should tie the decision to capacity headroom and model-family (large generation jobs vs short embed jobs). when headroom < 10% we should still page.
leo: what about grouping? can we group by node_pool + gpu_type + az so one page covers flapping across similar machines?
nana_p: small nit: grouping helps but make sure runbook points to "scale down faulty fleet" vs "restart nodes". oncall confusion last night — they tried manual scale before checking drain state.
sam_oncall: real ops perspective: 15m quiet window seems OK, but prefer 10m during business hours and 30m overnight. we get delayed responses at night and don't want repeated noise.
alex_w: good call. propose: 10m mute weekdays 08:00-20:00 in region local time, 30m otherwise. add an override tag for dedicated capacity contracts (they stay paging).
srebot: incident-bot: alertgroup "gpu_oom_v2" triggered 7 times in eu-west-1 between 02:14 and 02:42. avg resolution 3m (restart), peak pending pages: 4.
maya_k: also we should add a PromQL change: if we switch to ticketing we want an accompanying long-window alert for capacity loss and SLO breaches. here's a draft PromQL to detect sustained loss: 
```
sum by(node_pool) (gpu_available_capacity{region="eu-west-1"}) < (sum by(node_pool) (gpu_capacity{region="eu-west-1"}) * 0.9)
```
and then combine with an increase() over 10m for pages or OOM errors.
leo: can we also surface this on the SLO dashboard as a rolling headroom heatmap? ops looks at p95 latency but not raw headroom often.
manually: we should add a Grafana panel: headroom % by region, and a single-click "create ticket" action with prefilled diagnostics.
nana_p: runbook snippet suggestion: include `kubectl get nodes -l node_pool=<pool> -o wide` and `journalctl -u inference-service --since "-15m"` in the ticket template. saved time last night.
sam_oncall: cost question — if we mute noisy OOMs and rely on ticketing, are we risking customer impact that increases spend (failover to larger instances)? want explicit tie to cost alerts.
maya_k: agreed. add a companion metric: `cost_per_request` or at least `dedicated_fallback_count` and alert if fallback count > 5 within 1h along with headroom < 10%. that one should page.
alex_w: summary of proposed policy: 
- classify OOM alerts: transient (single-node restart <5m) -> ticketing + grouped, non-transient -> page
- mute window: 10m daytime / 30m night, region-local times
- override: dedicated capacity customers always page
- group by node_pool+gpu_type+az
- guardrails: if headroom <10% for 5m OR fallback_count >5 in 1h -> page and trigger capacity-runbook
- add Grafana panels and ticket-template with diagnostic commands
anyone want to take PR for alert-manager rules I can review?
leo: I can take the Prometheus rule change and grafana panel. will open PR today.
nana_p: I'll update the runbook and ticket template.
sam_oncall: I'll coordinate oncall settings and test the quiet windows in staging.
srebot: deploy-bot: alerting-rule "gpu-oom-smart-routing" staged to staging-alerts namespace by leo at 10:12.
alex_w: thanks all — aim to roll to prod after testing tomorrow. :thumbsup:
